chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus; and from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, all together from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:

Yūnus said: I presented the book to him, and he said: “It is sound.” And Ibn Faḍḍāl said: He said: “Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled that when a man is injured in one of his eyes, it is measured by an egg; his injured eye is bound, and it is observed how far the sight of his sound eye reaches. Then his sound eye is covered, and it is observed how far his injured eye reaches, and its compensation is given according to that calculation.

And al-qasāmah along with that is from six portions, according to the extent of what was injured from his eye. If it is one-sixth of his sight, he alone swears and is given compensation. If it is one-third of his sight, he swears and one man swears with him. If it is half of his sight, he swears and two men swear with him. If it is two-thirds of his sight, he swears and three men swear with him. If it is five-sixths of his sight, he swears and four men swear with him. If it is all of his sight, he swears and five men swear with him. Likewise is all al-qasāmah in wounds. If the injured one has no one to swear with him regarding his sight, the oaths are multiplied upon him: if it is one-sixth of his sight, he swears once; if it is one-third of his sight, he swears twice; and according to this reckoning. Al-qasāmah is only according to the extent reached by the limit of his sight.

And if it is hearing, then it is in a similar manner, except that something is struck for him until the limit of his hearing is known, then it is measured from that, and al-qasāmah is according to the manner of what is diminished from his hearing. If it is all of his hearing and immorality is feared from him, then he is left until, when sleep weighs heavily upon him, he is shouted at; if he hears, the judge assesses between the two by his judgment.

And if the deficiency is in the upper arm or the thigh, then the extent of that is determined. His sound leg is measured with a string, then the injured one is measured by it, and the amount by which his leg or hand has diminished is known. If the shin or the forearm is injured, it is measured from the thigh and the upper arm, and the judge considers the measure of his thigh.”

key_terms.الْجُرُوحِ: wounds and bodily injuries subject to legal assessment
key_terms.الْحَاكِمُ: the judge who evaluates and rules in the matter
key_terms.الْعَضُدِ: the upper arm as a bodily limb considered in assessment
key_terms.الْفَخِذِ: the thigh used as a reference in measuring injury
key_terms.اَلْقَسَامَةُ: a formal oath procedure used in adjudicating injury claims
key_terms.بَصَرِهِ: his faculty of sight as measured for legal compensation
key_terms.دِيَتُهُ: his financial compensation for the injury
key_terms.سَمْعِهِ: his faculty of hearing as measured for legal compensation

ai.seo_question: How does Shia fiqh assess compensation and al-qasāmah for injuries to sight, hearing, and limbs?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling attributed to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning the assessment of bodily injury, especially loss in sight, hearing, and limb proportion. It explains how compensation and al-qasāmah are determined according to measurable loss, showing a structured judicial method in bodily injury cases.
